bibleSpine.kjv: Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.
bibleSpine.gloss: The Bible's own definition: sin IS the transgression of the law — a committed act against a known standard, not a condition of birth.

bibleSpine.kjv: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.
bibleSpine.gloss: Sin's genealogy: temptation (lust) is not yet sin; sin is BORN only when lust CONCEIVES — when the will consents. The bent solicits; the consent births the sin.

bibleSpine.kjv: The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.
bibleSpine.gloss: Guilt is personal and non-transferable. No man is charged with another's iniquity — the flat rejection of inherited GUILT.

bibleSpine.kjv: Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.
bibleSpine.gloss: God claims every soul directly; each dies for its own sin, not the parent's — guilt attaches to the sinner, not the lineage.

bibleSpine.kjv: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: The judicial principle behind Ezekiel: every man dies for his OWN sin. Inherited guilt is foreign to God's law.

bibleSpine.kjv: Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.
bibleSpine.gloss: Every mouth is stopped — but the ground of guilt is stated in v.23: because all have actually SINNED, not because all were born.

bibleSpine.kjv: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
bibleSpine.gloss: The universal indictment rests on ACTS — 'all have sinned' (an active verb), the reason every mouth is stopped.

bibleSpine.kjv: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:
bibleSpine.gloss: Death passed upon all — not because all inherited Adam's guilt, but 'for that all have sinned.' The universal reign of death traces to universal actual sinning, made possible by the fallen nature Adam introduced.

bibleSpine.kjv: Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.
bibleSpine.gloss: The inherited CORRUPTION is real: David is bent from birth. This is a fallen nature, not a charged crime — a condition to be delivered from, not a guilt to be sentenced for.

bibleSpine.kjv: Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'By nature children of wrath' — the fallen nature is real and universal; note wrath is bound up with 'fulfilling the desires' — the nature condemns when obeyed, not merely possessed.

bibleSpine.kjv: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: The natural man is 'sold under sin' — the fallen nature holds dominion, a slavery, not a mere guilt-tag.

bibleSpine.kjv: Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me. For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.
bibleSpine.gloss: Paul distinguishes the indwelling 'sin' in the flesh from the willing self — the nature is a resident power, corrupting but not identical with the person's guilt.

bibleSpine.kjv: But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'A law in my members' — the inherited bent operates as a law of the nature, warring and taking captive; it enslaves the natural man.

bibleSpine.kjv: O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: The nature is not a life sentence: deliverance comes 'through Jesus Christ.' The bent enslaves UNTIL Christ delivers — corruption is curable, guilt would not be.

bibleSpine.kjv: Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ ties bondage to the COMMITTING of sin — the servitude of sin follows the act, and the fallen nature's dominion is broken by the Son (v.36).

symbolDefs.meaning: The consented transgression of God's law — a chosen act against a known standard, born when desire conceives (the will yields). It is defined by the law, not by birth; guilt attaches to the choice, never to the mere presence of a fallen inclination.
receipts: 1 John 3:4 — 'sin is the transgression of the law'
James 1:14-15 — sin is brought forth only 'when lust hath conceived,' i.e. when the will consents
John 8:34 — 'Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin' (the act, not the inheritance)
Ezekiel 18:20 — 'the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father' (guilt is personal, tied to one's own sinning)
Romans 3:23 — 'all have sinned' (the ground of universal guilt is the act)

symbolDefs.meaning: The inherited corruption — a real, terrible bent that inclines toward evil and holds dominion over the natural man, enslaving him until Christ delivers. It is 'sin that dwelleth in me' as a resident power, but it is NOT itself guilt; it condemns only when obeyed. Corruption inherited: affirmed. Guilt inherited: denied.
receipts: Psalm 51:5 — 'shapen in iniquity' (the nature is fallen from birth)
Ephesians 2:3 — 'by nature the children of wrath' (fallen nature universal), yet the wrath is joined to 'fulfilling the desires'
Romans 7:14 — 'carnal, sold under sin' (the nature enslaves)
Romans 7:17-18 — 'sin that dwelleth in me... in my flesh' distinguished from the willing self
Romans 7:23 — 'a law in my members' warring and bringing into captivity
Romans 7:24-25 — deliverance 'through Jesus Christ' (the bent enslaves only until Christ frees)

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: "Whosoever committeth sin," he writes, "transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law."
witnesses.gloss: White lets John define sin as she cites 1 John 3:4 verbatim — sin is the transgression of the law, an act, dealt with 'in plain terms' as a doing.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Well, you say, it was Adam's sin. You say, I am not guilty of that, and I am not responsible for his guilt and fall. Here all these natural tendencies are in me and I am not to blame if I act out these natural tendencies. Who is to blame? Is God?
witnesses.gloss: White's 1888 Minneapolis sermon holds BOTH sides exactly as the section requires: we are not guilty of Adam's fall (inherited guilt denied), yet the natural fallen tendencies are really 'in me' (corruption affirmed) — and we ARE to blame if we act them out (guilt at consent).

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: There is no sin in having temptation, but sin comes in when temptation is yielded to.
witnesses.gloss: The precise James 1:14-15 distinction: the solicitation of the fallen nature is not sin; sin is born at the yielding of the will.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: It is Satan's act to tempt you, but your own act to yield. It is not in the power of all the host of Satan to force the tempted to transgress. There is no excuse for sin.
witnesses.gloss: Guilt is located at the personal act of yielding, not the presence of temptation — no inherited or external force compels transgression; the consent is one's own.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: An impure thought tolerated, an unholy desire cherished, and the soul is contaminated... "Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death." If we would not commit sin, we must shun its very beginnings.
witnesses.gloss: White quotes James 1:15 and traces the birth of sin from a cherished/tolerated desire (the will's consent) to the act — sin conceived by the will, not by birth.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: This is the governing power in the nature of man—the power of decision, of choice. Everything depends on the right action of the will... Many will go down to ruin while hoping and desiring to overcome their evil propensities. They do not yield the will to God.
witnesses.gloss: The will is the deciding power; guilt and ruin turn on its action, not on the mere existence of 'evil propensities' — desires alone 'avail nothing.' Confirms guilt attaches to choice, not to the inherited bent.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Those who put their trust in Christ are not to be enslaved by any hereditary or cultivated habit or tendency. Instead of being held in bondage to the lower nature... Whatever may be our inherited or cultivated tendencies to wrong, we can overcome through the power that He is ready to impart.
witnesses.gloss: Names the inherited tendency as real bondage of the 'lower nature' (corruption affirmed) that ENSLAVES until Christ delivers — precisely the bent that is not itself guilt but can be overcome.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: the flesh which He assumed had all the weaknesses and sinful tendencies to which fallen human nature is subject... David had all the passions of human nature. He says of himself, "Behold I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me." Psalm 51:5.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner establishes the reality of the inherited fallen nature from Psalm 51:5 — the flesh carries 'weaknesses and sinful tendencies' — while (in the same argument) never conceding actual sin. Corruption real, tendencies inherited.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: We likewise can all say, with David, "Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me." ... As a consequence, we are by nature so weak that we cannot do the things that we would.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner reads Psalm 51:5 as the confession of an inherited weakness of nature that disables ('cannot do the things that we would' — echoing Rom. 7) — a bent to be delivered from by Christ's power, not a charged guilt.

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: when a man is converted... he is not so delivered from the flesh that he is actually separated from it with its tendencies and desires... No, that same degenerate, sinful flesh is there with its same tendencies and desires. But the individual is no longer subject to these... a power that conquers, brings under, crucifies, and keeps under, the flesh, sinful as it is, with all its affections and lusts.
witnesses.gloss: Jones states the whole section's thesis on the flesh: the inherited 'degenerate, sinful flesh' with its tendencies REMAINS even in the converted — a real bent — but the man is 'no longer subject' to it; the Spirit keeps it under. Corruption inherited and enslaving, yet conquerable, not guilt.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: "I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind..." ... This sin is in our flesh... But we are slaves. Whosoever commits sin is the slave of sin. John 8:34. Therefore it is that the law that will not let us be anything but what we are, is really holding us in bondage.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner expounds Romans 7:23 — the 'law in my members' is sin dwelling in the flesh that holds the natural man in bondage/slavery (linking John 8:34). The fallen nature is a dominion that enslaves until liberty comes in Christ.

historyAnchor: White's clearest statement of this exact distinction (not guilty of Adam's fall, yet the natural tendencies are really in us) was preached at the 1888 Minneapolis General Conference session (Ms 8, 1888 = 1MR 142.3), the same watershed session where Waggoner and Jones pressed righteousness by faith.
uncertainties: The classic short EGW maxim commonly quoted as 'There is no sin in having temptations, but sin comes in when temptation is yielded to' resolves verbatim only in HP 251.3 (and near-identically in ST May 27, 1897, par. 3); other memory-quoted forms may not match the corpus exactly.

Several precise LtMs paragraph refcodes (e.g. '21LtMs, Lt 376, 1906, par. 32'; '5LtMs, Ms 8, 1888, par. 6') could not be retrieved by direct lookup because the comma in the refcode trips the local FTS parser; the 1888 sermon content was verified instead through its parallel release 1MR 142.3, which is cited.

Romans 5:12 ('for that all have sinned') is read here in the Greek/Arminian sense that death spread because all actually sinned; a federal-headship (imputed-guilt) reading of the same verse is deliberately not adopted, consistent with Ezek. 18:20 and Deut. 24:16 — this is an interpretive stance, not a bare quotation.
